thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High decode tail latency detected (p99) in cluster us-west1-gpu. AlertID=ALRT-1770018. paging=true. Metric spike started ~1770017980.
oncall-amber: I'm oncall, looking. Confirming the p99 jump on streaming-decode route. p95 went from ~300ms to ~920ms, p99 ~700ms -> ~2.3s. Seeing an increase in RPC retries and stalled streams.
linus: noted. Any recent kernel or driver rollouts? I saw a small rollout this morning to kernel 535.86 on a subset of nodes. TRT runtime was also bumped in some arenas yesterday (trt 9.1).
maya: kv-cache eviction rate spiked around the same time, and prefix cache hit-rate dropped 18%. Could be memory/locking regression causing page faults.
alex: quick triage checklist: 1) identify nodes with kernel 535.86 2) isolate traffic 3) rollback kernel to 535.70 if confirmed 4) enable fallback model variant if needed.
eng-runtime: running node query now. 
eng-runtime: command: ```rbctl nodes list --region us-west1 --filter "kernel=535.86" | wc -l``` -> 120 nodes (about 28% of pool).
eng-runtime: correlating with p99 by host: ```promql: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(decode_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))``` shows hosts with kernel=535.86 have elevated tail.
oncall-amber: OK let's put traffic away from those hosts. Can we route a small % to dedicated pool with older kernel?
alex: yes. Temporary routing: ```redwood route set --service streaming-decode --weight fallback-pool=0.15 --selector "kernel=535.70" --comment "oncall 1770018 mitigation"``` Start with 15%.
eng-runtime: applied route -> 15% diverted. Metrics: p95 drops slightly after diversion, p99 still high but trending down on some shards.
linus: even with 15% diverted, p99 still >1.8s on impacted hosts. Suggest rolling rollback of kernel on impacted hosts rather than full fleet restart.
maya: I can prepare a kexec rollback plan. We should coordinate with SRE for safe draining to avoid evictions.
sre-lead: Agreed. Runbook steps I'm executing now:
1) Mark impacted hosts as drain candidates: ```infractl host annotate --hosts $(nodes list --kernel=535.86) --tag drain-oncall-1770018```
2) Rollback kernel package to 535.70 and reboot in rolling batches of 10 hosts: ```infractl host update-kernel --batch-size 10 --version 535.70 --reboot true --parallel 2```
3) Verify prefix-cache hitrate and decode p99 after each batch; abort if regressions.
4) If rollback not possible quickly, increase per-request timeouts and enable extra retry/backoff at LB to reduce customer-facing stalls.

sre-lead: kicking off batch 1 (10 hosts). ETA ~6m per batch incl. drain and cordon.
oncall-amber: Noted. Starting customer impact & comms: Bob, can you flag any high-touch customers seeing errors?
customer-success-bob: Yep — account: AcmeAI reported streaming stalls and timeouts starting ~09:18 PST. I've opened a ticket and notified their SRE. Also seeing elevated error reports from RetailGen.
linus: also observed increased soft pagefaults in kernel logs on impacted hosts: ```dmesg | tail -n 50``` showing repetitive: "page allocation failure" and backtrace pointing to vm_lock path. That aligns with cache eviction surge.
maya: preliminary hypothesis: kernel 535.86 changed page reclaim heuristics which interacts poorly with our pinned GPU mmap usage -> increased stalls and KV cache churn.
alex: mitigation status: route diversion at 15% applied, batch1 rollback started. Please capture perf dump if any host fails to come up.
eng-runtime: batch1 completed, post-rollback p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~560ms on those hosts. Good signal. Proceeding with batch2.
sre-lead: rolling through batches, observing consistent improvement as batches finish. Current global p99: 1.05s, p95: 420ms.
oncall-amber: keep me posted. Also create short-term alert to trigger if p99 > 1.5s for more than 2m so we can auto-pause rollout.
eng-runtime: added alert: ALERT-1770018-TAKEOVER when decode_p99 > 1.5s for 2m.
linus: note for postmortem: need to repro in staging with kernel 535.86 + our heavy kv/prefix workload; add vmalloc stress tests.
maya: adding a guardrail to our rollout pipeline: don't bump kernels outside of canary_bay unless prefix-cache hitrate delta < 5% for 30m.
customer-success-bob: customers updated. AcmeAI acknowledged the heads-up and appreciates the timely mitigation. No SLA hits yet recorded but monitoring continues.
oncall-amber: Summary for incident log: cause suspected kernel page reclaim regression introduced in kernel 535.86, correlated with KV cache evictions and elevated soft pagefaults leading to decode tail spikes on ~28% of nodes. Mitigation: diverted 15% traffic to fallback pool, performed rolling kernel rollback to 535.70 across impacted hosts, monitored metrics; p99 reduced to ~420-560ms on rolled hosts; global p99 trending to normal.
eng-runtime: leaving this thread open for handoff to postmortem. Owner: linus (root cause), maya (repro/test), alex (deployment pipeline guardrails), sre-lead (rollback/runbook updates), customer-success-bob (customer comms).
linus: assigning postmortem ticket PMT-1770018, will include timeline, kernel diff, and repro steps.
oncall-amber: thanks everyone, nice coordination. Reacts: :thumbsup: :coffee:
incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation at 1770019345 — monitoring only. For postmortem scheduling, see PMT-1770018.
